elements.requirement: A person has a duty to have regard to any relevant code if that person is acting in relation to a person who lacks capacity as the donee of a lasting power of attorney.
elements.quote: It is the duty of a person to have regard to any relevant code if he is acting in relation to a person who lacks capacity and is doing so in one or more of the following ways— (a) as the donee of a lasting power of attorney

elements.requirement: A person has a duty to have regard to any relevant code if that person is acting in relation to a person who lacks capacity as a deputy appointed by the court.
elements.quote: It is the duty of a person to have regard to any relevant code if he is acting in relation to a person who lacks capacity and is doing so in one or more of the following ways— (b) as a deputy appointed by the court

elements.requirement: A person has a duty to have regard to any relevant code if that person is acting in relation to a person who lacks capacity as a person carrying out research in reliance on any provision made by or under the Act pursuant to sections 30 to 34.
elements.quote: It is the duty of a person to have regard to any relevant code if he is acting in relation to a person who lacks capacity and is doing so in one or more of the following ways— (c) as a person carrying out research in reliance on any provision made by or under this Act (see sections 30 to 34)

elements.requirement: A person has a duty to have regard to any relevant code if that person is acting in relation to a person who lacks capacity as an independent mental capacity advocate.
elements.quote: It is the duty of a person to have regard to any relevant code if he is acting in relation to a person who lacks capacity and is doing so in one or more of the following ways— (d) as an independent mental capacity advocate

elements.requirement: A person has a duty to have regard to any relevant code if that person is acting in relation to a person who lacks capacity in a professional capacity.

elements.requirement: A person has a duty to have regard to any relevant code if that person is acting in relation to a person who lacks capacity for remuneration.
elements.quote: It is the duty of a person to have regard to any relevant code if he is acting in relation to a person who lacks capacity and is doing so in one or more of the following ways— (f) for remuneration

elements.requirement: A court or tribunal conducting any criminal or civil proceedings must take into account a provision of a code or a failure to comply with a code when deciding a question arising in the proceedings, if that provision or failure appears relevant to the question.
elements.quote: If it appears to a court or tribunal conducting any criminal or civil proceedings that— (a) a provision of a code, or (b) a failure to comply with a code, is relevant to a question arising in the proceedings, the provision or failure must be taken into account in deciding the question.

elements.requirement: A code prepared for the guidance of deputies appointed by the court is permitted to contain separate guidance for deputies appointed by virtue of paragraph 1(2) of Schedule 5 where functions of a deputy are conferred on a receiver appointed under the Mental Health Act.
elements.quote: A code under subsection (1)(d) may contain separate guidance for deputies appointed by virtue of paragraph 1(2) of Schedule 5 (functions of deputy conferred on receiver appointed under the Mental Health Act).

elements.requirement: In section 42 and in section 43 of the Act, the term 'code' is defined as a code prepared or revised under section 42.
elements.quote: In this section and in section 43, “code” means a code prepared or revised under this section.
